inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted, FY2026 10-K balance sheet (shares outstanding 114.0M at 2026-06-30, matching the 2026-07-31 cover-page count of 114.02M); held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in owner FCF (charging both would double-count). Down from 117.1M a year earlier on FY2026's $603.7M buyback.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 10-K (filed 2026-08-04) cash flow statement: Stock-based compensation expense add-back $93.9M. BR publishes no combined SBC+equity-award-tax reconciliation figure (its non-GAAP 'Adjusted' measures do not add back SBC at all), so per method (a) the cash-tax-withholding-on-vesting outflow is summed separately: 'Other financing activities' in financing activities, $25.1M FY2026 ($21.6M FY2025, $14.3M FY2024), read as the RSU net-share-settlement tax withholding (the 10-K's equity-award note states shares withheld for payroll taxes on RSU vesting are treated as treasury stock but excluded from the disclosed 'shares repurchased under the share repurchase program' count, implying a separate cash line from 'Purchases of Treasury stock'). Combined sbc_incl_equity_taxes = 93.9 + 25.1 = 119.0.
inputs.wacc_rationale: 8.5% for a US investment-grade fintech/business-services compounder with moderate leverage (net debt/EBITDA ~1.6x on ebitda-before-SBC), stable >95% recurring-revenue retention, and no material FX or emerging-market risk premium beyond the standard US ERP.
inputs.lease_treatment: Not material — BR's lease footprint (offices, print/mail facilities) is small relative to revenue; no separate lease adjustment applied; operating lease cost stays inside SG&A/opex embedded in the EBITDA margin.
inputs.nci_treatment: None — Broadridge has no minority interests in its consolidated group.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF DCF, standard operating-company route (fintech/business-process services; near-monopoly US proxy distribution/vote tabulation plus capital-markets and wealth-management technology outsourcing). Routed via .claude/skills/dcf-methods/SKILL.md; no owner-fcf-adaptations needed (US filer, USD flows and quote, no leases/NCI/non-operating assets of consequence). FY2026 reported_fcf corrected from the CSV's FreeCashFlow (which nets only the 'Capital expenditures' line) to the company's own Free Cash Flow non-GAAP definition, which also deducts 'Software purchases and capitalized internal use software' ($45.4M FY2026): OCF $1,345.6M - total capex $112.6M (=67.2+45.4) = $1,233.0M, tying to the 10-K's disclosed Free cash flow of $1,233.0M. capex_pct_path therefore uses TOTAL capex (hardware + capitalized software), not the CSV's narrower capex column. D&A includes both owned-asset D&A ($137.7M) and amortization of acquired intangibles/purchased IP ($203.6M) — the latter is a real economic cost of BR's acquisitive growth strategy (Acolin, Signal, iJoin, CQG) and is kept in the D&A line rather than added back. FY2026 net income included a $227.0M non-cash 'Gains on Digital Assets' item (Canton Coin/Canton Digital Asset Treasury) that does not touch OCF and is excluded from the owner-FCF build entirely since the build starts from OCF, not net income. Cash tax rate: FY2026's cash-taxes/pretax-income ratio (14.1%) is depressed by the one-off digital-asset gain's tax treatment; the model uses the steadier GAAP effective tax rate (~20-22% actual, ramping to 23% mid-build) as the cash tax proxy rather than perpetuating the low FY2026 print. Net debt is materially positive (~$2.85bn), so interest income is not stripped from FCF (this is a net-debt, not net-cash, company).

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: equity_5yr_cagr, blended toward revenue CAGR and management's stated 6-8% recurring-revenue algorithm
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF CAGR (19.2%, FY2023-FY2026, computed on the company's own total-capex FCF definition net of SBC-incl-equity-taxes) runs well ahead of the 7.25% revenue CAGR over the same window — this is genuine margin expansion (owner-FCF margin 10.9% -> 14.9% over three years) driven by fixed print/postage/tech infrastructure operating leverage plus the FY2026 one-off digital-asset tax/timing benefit, not a sign SBC is outrunning cash flow (SBC-to-revenue is a low and stable ~1.1-1.3%, unlike heavy-SBC tech issuers). Net income and diluted-EPS CAGRs (21.3%/15.5%) are further inflated by FY2026's non-cash $227.0M digital-asset gain and the buyback-driven falling share count; the DCF anchors growth on equity CAGR (9.4% 5yr) and revenue, not on the EPS series, and management's own long-term algorithm (6-8% recurring revenue, 8-12% adjusted EPS growth) is used to calibrate the base case rather than extrapolating the inflated trailing print. No revenue/equity divergence flag: 8.4% vs 9.4% is well within the 30% threshold.

base.narrative: FY2027 growth (~6%) reflects the guided 6-8% recurring-revenue algorithm net of event-driven revenue normalizing to $250-300M from FY2026's record $348M (a ~1pp drag on total growth). Growth holds at management's stated 6-8% algorithm through the middle years as the $470M closed-sales backlog converts, then decelerates toward a 2.5% terminal rate as the US proxy/governance base (already processing >80% of outstanding US shares) matures and event-driven volatility averages out. EBITDA margin (before SBC) rises gradually from the current 23.2% toward a 25% mature level as digital-communications mix shift and AI-driven productivity gains (management's own ~$25M FY2027 estimate) offset print/postage cost inflation, consistent with the guided ~21% adjusted operating margin path. SBC-to-revenue stays low and roughly flat given BR's historically modest equity-comp intensity. D&A-to-revenue drifts down slowly as the acquisition-intangible amortization schedule (CQG, Acolin, Signal, iJoin) runs off faster than new deals are layered on. Cash tax rate ramps from the depressed FY2026 print (distorted by the one-off digital-asset gain) to a steady 23% blended US federal/state rate.

bull.narrative: Tokenization/digital-asset infrastructure (NYFIX crypto/tokenized-asset order routing, ~$7.5tn monthly tokenized-repo volume) and agentic-AI productivity tools become genuine new growth legs rather than optionality, event-driven revenue normalizes at the high end of guidance, and the bolt-on M&A strategy (following CQG, Acolin, Signal, iJoin) continues to add adjacent capability without over-levering. GTO outsourcing tailwinds persist as AI raises rather than lowers the value of Broadridge's shared infrastructure for banks and wealth managers. Margin expands further as digital-communications mix shift and AI cost productivity compound, supporting a premium exit multiple in line with the business's historical trading range.

bear.narrative: Event-driven revenue drops toward the low end of the $250-300M guided range and stays structurally lower as proxy-contest and M&A-driven special-meeting activity remains subdued; physical-mail decline and USPS postage inflation outrun the digital-communications offset, pressuring Customer Communications economics. GTO outsourcing growth stalls as AI enables large capital-markets and wealth-management clients to insource technology rather than pay Broadridge, and integration friction across the recent acquisition pace (Acolin, Signal, iJoin, CQG) absorbs management attention without delivering the expected cross-sell. Elevated leverage (~$3.25bn debt) becomes a binding constraint on further bolt-on M&A in a higher-for-longer rate environment, and the business settles into a slower-growing, margin-flat utility rather than a compounder, closing some of today's premium valuation gap.

scenario_narratives.base: Long-term 6-8% recurring-revenue / 8-12% adjusted-EPS algorithm holds, event-driven revenue normalizes from FY2026's record level but does not collapse, and gradual digital/AI-driven margin expansion continues the multi-year trend from a 23% toward a 25% mature EBITDA-before-SBC margin.
scenario_narratives.bull: Tokenization and agentic-AI initiatives become real incremental growth drivers rather than optionality, event-driven revenue lands at the high end of guidance, and disciplined bolt-on M&A keeps expanding TAM without over-levering — supporting both faster growth and margin expansion.
scenario_narratives.bear: Event-driven revenue settles at the low end of guidance and stays there, AI-enabled insourcing pressures GTO's outsourcing thesis, postage/print cost inflation outruns the digital offset, and elevated leverage constrains further M&A — the business becomes a slower, margin-flat utility.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: House default nudged toward base (55% vs the standard 50%) given the multi-year track record of hitting the stated 6-8%/8-12% growth algorithm, >95% recurring-revenue retention, and a near-monopoly regulatory position in US proxy distribution that structurally caps how far the bear case can run. Bear weight held slightly above the 15% floor (20%) for the event-driven-revenue normalization risk flagged explicitly in FY2027 guidance and the AI-insourcing risk to GTO, which are real but not going-concern-level risks. Bull weight trimmed to 25% because the tokenization/agentic-AI upside requires several distinct things (regulatory clarity on digital assets, actual monetization of NYFIX volumes, AI cost savings materializing beyond the guided $25M) to go right simultaneously.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Broadridge is a high-quality, recession-resistant infrastructure compounder: near-monopoly US proxy distribution/vote tabulation (>80% of outstanding US shares) generates deeply entrenched, contractually recurring revenue with >95% retention, supplemented by capital-markets and wealth-management technology outsourcing (GTO) and a volatile but historically self-funding event-driven revenue stream. The owner-FCF DCF values the durable cash-generative core rather than crediting the stock's premium market multiple, and discounts a decade-long build because the owner-FCF margin (10.9% -> 14.9% over the last three years) is still climbing toward a mature level, not yet flat.
key_risks_to_valuation: Event-driven revenue (proxy contests, M&A-driven special meetings, mutual fund communications spikes) is inherently unpredictable and management itself guides it down 14-28% for FY2027 off a record FY2026
Elevated leverage (~$3.25bn total debt, ~$2.85bn net debt) from an active bolt-on M&A pace increases refinancing and integration risk
AI could eventually enable large capital-markets/wealth-management clients to insource GTO's outsourced technology and operations rather than continuing to pay Broadridge
Structural decline of physical mail and rising USPS postage costs pressure legacy Customer Communications economics during the digital transition
The stock trades at a premium multiple (~19x owner FCF) that leaves limited room for execution missteps or a capital-markets slowdown
